title: Piedmontese hazelnut cake (torta di nocciole)
summary: A plain, fragrant single-layer cake made almost entirely of toasted ground hazelnuts, eggs and a little butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 °C (340 °F). Grease a 23 cm (9 in) round pan and line the base with parchment.
If using hazelnut flour, toast it in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until it smells nutty, about 4 minutes; tip it out to cool. Whisk in the baking powder and salt.
Whisk the yolks with half the erythritol until pale and thick, then whisk in the melted butter, vanilla and almond milk. Stir in the hazelnut mixture.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the rest of the erythritol and whisk until firm. Fold into the hazelnut batter in three additions.
Spread in the pan, scatter the chopped hazelnuts over and bake 30–35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then turn out and cool on a rack. Dust with powdered erythritol to serve.

swaps.note: melted; or a mild olive oil

dairy_free_notes: Made with coconut oil or olive oil the cake is just as moist; olive oil keeps it softer in the fridge, where coconut oil firms up.
tips: Toasting the nuts is what gives the cake its flavour; do not skip it.

origin.history: The Langhe hills of southern Piedmont are known for the Tonda Gentile hazelnut, and a simple cake of ground hazelnuts is a long-standing farmhouse dessert there; its exact date of origin is not recorded. The same nuts later underpinned Piedmont's gianduja chocolate and the region's hazelnut confectionery industry.
